deed: IsraAID שלח 20 אנשי חילוץ, סיוע וטראומה לרעידת האדמה באמטריצ'ה שבאיטליה
title: IsraAID sent 20 rescue, relief and trauma personnel to the earthquake in Amatrice, Italy

trailer.text: IsraAID is an international non-governmental humanitarian organization based in Israel; it was founded in 2001 and, according to its website, has worked in more than 60 countries.
According to IsraAID, on August 24, 2016, a 6.2 magnitude earthquake struck central Italy.
According to Israel21c, on the night of August 25 the Israeli organization sent a 20-member delegation: a search-and-rescue squad, relief workers and trauma specialists.
According to Israel21c, the Israelis built temporary shelter camps, distributed food, and counseled grieving families and Italian rescue teams.
According to IsraAID, in the years after 2016 the organization remained on the ground and worked with its partner Legacoop Lazio to strengthen disaster preparedness and resilience in the community.

glance.label: Organization
glance.value: IsraAID, a humanitarian organization from Israel

glance.label: Where
glance.value: IsraAID announced that its team would focus on the towns of Amatrice, Pescara del Tronto and Accumoli.

glance.value: 20 search and rescue, relief and trauma personnel

paragraphs.text: According to Ynetnews, at least 40 aftershocks were felt in cities such as Rome, Naples and Florence.
According to IsraAID, in the first hours the authorities struggled to reach the rural area, and it was not clear how many people were still buried.
According to the Jerusalem Post, there were reports of voices of survivors beneath the rubble, but the area is remote, and officials sometimes lack heavy equipment that can move the large stones.
According to Ynet, by noon on the day of the earthquake the death toll already stood at 38, and about 150 people were missing.
According to Israel21c, in Amatrice alone 230 residents and tourists were killed.
According to Israel21c, the youngest victim was five months old and the oldest was 93.
According to an IsraAID report, more than 4,000 people were displaced from their homes in the regions of Lazio, Marche, Umbria and Abruzzo.
According to IsraAID, after the extensive damage and the aftershocks there were fears of psychological harm to children and to entire communities.
IsraAID announced that it would immediately send a relief and rescue team to the affected areas, and that the team would focus on the towns of Amatrice, Pescara del Tronto and Accumoli.
According to the organization, the team planned to work in three areas: search and rescue, emergency aid and psychosocial support.
According to Israel21c, the 20-member delegation set out on the night of August 25.
According to an IsraAID report, the team arrived less than 36 hours after the earthquake.
According to Shachar Zahavi, the organization's founder and director, the organization was able to send the team thanks to the support of The Ted Arison Family Foundation.
According to The Jewish Link, Prime Minister Netanyahu offered to send search-and-rescue and recovery teams from the IDF to Italy.

stations.title: On the ground: shelter, food and a warm blanket

paragraphs.text: According to the Jerusalem Post, the team members wore blue and orange and worked alongside their Italian counterparts.
According to Israel21c, the Israelis built temporary shelter camps and distributed food and other items.
According to a member of the IsraAID team, one of the community shelters in the area was set up within 24 hours of the quake; the source does not say who set it up.
According to eJewishPhilanthropy, Scai is a small village whose residents are mostly elderly, and at least 80 of its residents sought safety in the community shelter.
According to team member Miki Noam Alon, Gabriele Gabiza, 82, was asleep at home when the earthquake hit it; part of the house collapsed and the walls cracked.
According to Noam Alon, a member of the organization's team helped Gabiza find a place to sit and brought him a warm blanket and water.
According to Ynetnews, psychologist Silvana Winer, who was born in Rome and immigrated to Israel at age 20, was among the first recruited to the team.
According to Ynetnews, in Amatrice Winer worked in close coordination with the local Red Cross and the medical staff of the Carabinieri.
According to Ynetnews, her role was to stand alongside the rescue teams as bodies were uncovered, and to help families identify loved ones buried under the ruins.
According to Ynetnews, IsraAID's trauma therapists accompanied the families throughout the process, from the identification of the bodies to the decisions about burial and the funeral.
According to Israel21c, the team also counseled Italian rescue teams suffering from exhaustion and acute stress.
According to JTA, IsraAID brought to Italy from Israel a team of psychologists trained in dealing with the effects of post-traumatic stress disorder.
According to IsraAID, in such situations early psycho-social support is critical to recovery and to the prevention of trauma.
According to Ynetnews, psycho-social support and grief counseling are crucial to community resilience and to preventing post-traumatic stress disorder, although they are sometimes overlooked.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Italy's largest Jewish community, the community of Rome, began a blood drive and vowed to raise money for the victims of the earthquake.

According to JTA, a delegation of the Union of Italian Jewish Communities (UCEI) and IsraAID visited the earthquake zone and distributed thermal blankets, jackets, shoes and portable heaters to those left homeless by the summer and autumn quakes.

stations.title: Staying on: CoopAID and the mobile playroom

paragraphs.text: According to an IsraAID report, the organization committed to supporting the long-term recovery of Amatrice and the surrounding area.
According to IsraAID, the Lazio branch of Legacoop and the organization together created CoopAID, a collective intended to improve mental health and psychosocial support systems.
According to IsraAID, the organization's team in Amatrice operated the "play-mobile", a mobile playroom that travels from school to school and gives children a safe space to express their feelings.

According to IsraAID, much of the project was intended to strengthen local leaders, especially social workers and therapists, so that they could support a vulnerable population should another crisis break out.
According to IsraAID, together with the cooperative federation Legacoop, long-term training was planned for 30 volunteers in psychological support techniques and the promotion of recovery.
According to IsraAID, the CoopAID project was presented in the plenary session of the Legacoop National Conference, held in Rome in April.
According to GlobalGiving, the project, together with other sources of funding, raised enough money for the planned activities, and is therefore no longer accepting donations.
Anna, a social worker and the project manager at Legacoop Sociali Lazio, said that the training helped enhance the resources of the cooperatives and the network between staff members.
Massimo, a social worker from Calabria, said that IsraAID's training helped the participants understand how to manage their own emotions and those of others in a natural disaster.

disagreements.question: How many people were killed in the earthquake?

versions.says: The Jerusalem Post on August 27, 2016: at least 281 dead and hundreds more missing
Israel21c on August 28, 2016: 290 dead throughout the region
The Jewish Link on September 1, 2016: at least 267 dead, more than half of them in Amatrice

disagreements.question: How many people were sheltered in camps or left without a roof over their heads?

versions.says: Israel21c, citing the Italian Civil Protection: 2,500 people sheltered in displaced-persons camps
The Jewish Link, citing the Italian authorities: some 2,100 people took refuge in temporary camps
Ynet on the day of the earthquake: about 2,500 people left without a roof over their heads in Amatrice

disagreements.question: Did Italy request or receive aid from Israel?

versions.says: Ynet on the day of the earthquake: Israel offered aid, and Italy thanked it and made clear that it does not need it at present
The Jewish Link: following the offers of aid from Netanyahu and President Rivlin, an Israeli aid organization specializing in disasters arrived in Italy

disagreements.question: Was IsraAID the first foreign aid organization on the ground, or the only one?

versions.says: The Jerusalem Post, August 27, 2016: as of that date, the only foreign humanitarian aid organization on the ground that is non-governmental and non-profit.
Israel21c on August 28, 2016: currently the only foreign group of its kind helping the Italians on the ground
Ynetnews, citing Reuters: the organization was the first on the ground, the first foreign aid organization
The Jewish Link on September 1, 2016: the first foreign humanitarian aid organization to help local counterparts at the earthquake epicenter

claims.text: לפי Ynet ביום הרעידה, כ-2,500 בני אדם נותרו ללא קורת גג באמטריצ'ה והרשויות פרסו אוהלים ופינו חלק מהם לערים אחרות.
claims.quote: כ-2,500 בני אדם נותרו ללא קורת גג באמטריצ'ה, והרשויות פורסות באזור אוהלים ומפנות חלק מחסרי הבית לערים אחרות במרכז איטליה

claims.text: לפי Ynet ביום הרעידה, ישראל הציעה סיוע לאיטליה, אך איטליה הודתה על ההצעה והבהירה שאינה זקוקה לו כעת.
claims.quote: ישראל הציעה הבוקר לאיטליה סיוע בעקבות הרעש, אך איטליה הודתה על ההצעה והבהירה כי היא אינה זקוקה כעת לסיוע.

claims.text: לפי The Jewish Link, לאחר הצעות סיוע של ראש הממשלה נתניהו והנשיא ריבלין הגיע לאיטליה ארגון סיוע ישראלי המתמחה בהתמודדות עם אסונות.
claims.quote: Following offers of aid from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Reuven Rivlin, an Israeli humanitarian group specializing in disaster response has arrived in Italy

claims.text: לפי Israel21c ב-28 באוגוסט 2016, צוות IsraAID הוא כרגע הקבוצה הזרה היחידה מסוגה שעוזרת לעמיתים האיטלקים בשטח.
claims.quote: the IsraAID team currently is the only foreign group of its kind helping Italian counterparts on the ground in the wake of a 6.2 magnitude earthquake

claims.text: לפי Ynetnews (Reuters) מ-29 באוגוסט 2016, IsraAID, ארגון הסיוע הבינלאומי הישראלי, היה הראשון בשטח באיטליה אחרי הרעידה.
claims.quote: IsraAID, the Israeli international aid organization, was the first on the ground in Italy after the devastating earthquake there on August 24

claims.text: לפי Ynetnews, אנשי החירום של IsraAID היו בכוננות כבר בתוך שעות מהרעידה, והארגון היה ארגון הסיוע הזר הראשון בשטח.
claims.quote: IsraAID was the first foreign aid organization on the ground in Italy to help survivors.

claims.text: לפי The Jewish Link (TheTower) מ-1 בספטמבר 2016, צוות IsraAID בן 20 החברים היה ארגון הסיוע ההומניטרי הזר הראשון שעזר לעמיתים המקומיים באפיצנטר.
claims.quote: was the first foreign humanitarian NGO to help local counterparts with recovery efforts at the earthquake epicenter, Jewish Philanthropy reported.

quote_translations.c45: The death toll in the earthquake in central Italy rose at noon (Wednesday) to 38, but about 150 people are missing
quote_translations.c46: About 2,500 people were left without a roof over their heads in Amatrice, and the authorities are setting up tents in the area and evacuating some of the homeless to other cities in central Italy
quote_translations.c44: This morning Israel offered Italy aid following the quake, but Italy thanked it for the offer and made clear that it does not need aid at present.
